title: Albuterol Tablets, USP: prescribing information
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, approved labelling; DailyMed structured product labelling version 7, published 18 March 2026, text revised 03/2023
funder: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, Inc. distributes the product and submits the labelling text; the US Food and Drug Administration approves it.
result: Indicated for relief of bronchospasm in adults and children 6 years and older; usual adult dose 2 or 4 mg three or four times daily, total daily dose not above 32 mg. After one 4 mg tablet in normal volunteers, maximum plasma albuterol was about 18 ng/ml within 2 hours, with a half-life of about 5 hours. The most frequent adverse reactions in clinical trials were nervousness 20%, tremor 20%, headache 7%, tachycardia 5%, palpitations 5% and muscle cramps 3%. Warnings: paradoxical bronchospasm that may be life threatening; clinically significant cardiovascular effects, with electrocardiographic T-wave flattening, QTc prolongation and ST depression reported; immediate hypersensitivity reactions; rare erythema multiforme and Stevens-Johnson syndrome with oral albuterol in children; significant hypokalaemia; aggravation of pre-existing diabetes mellitus and ketoacidosis by large intravenous doses. Albuterol is not approved for preterm labour, and serious adverse reactions including maternal pulmonary oedema have been reported during or after treatment of premature labour with beta2-agonists including albuterol. Overdosage may produce seizures, angina, hypertension or hypotension, tachycardia up to 200 beats/min and arrhythmias; cardiac arrest and death may be associated with abuse. Subcutaneous albuterol produced cleft palate in 5 of 111 (4.5%) and 10 of 108 (9.3%) mouse fetuses at 0.25 and 2.5 mg/kg; congenital anomalies including cleft palate and limb defects have been rarely reported in offspring of treated patients without a consistent pattern.
